Topics · Prayer and closeness to God

Is it wrong to make a vow for someone sick?

A mother's vow, and Mary's own. Vows made in love are no lack in the Quran. God is near and answers.

Part 1 of 4

﴿إِذْ قَالَتِ ٱمْرَأَتُ عِمْرَٰنَ رَبِّ إِنِّى نَذَرْتُ لَكَ مَا فِى بَطْنِى مُحَرَّرًا فَتَقَبَّلْ مِنِّىٓ ۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلْعَلِيمُ٣٥ فَلَمَّا وَضَعَتْهَا قَالَتْ رَبِّ إِنِّى وَضَعْتُهَآ أُنثَىٰ وَٱللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِمَا وَضَعَتْ وَلَيْسَ ٱلذَّكَرُ كَٱلْأُنثَىٰ ۖ وَإِنِّى سَمَّيْتُهَا مَرْيَمَ وَإِنِّىٓ أُعِيذُهَا بِكَ وَذُرِّيَّتَهَا مِنَ ٱلشَّيْطَـٰنِ ٱلرَّجِيمِ٣٦ فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍ وَأَنۢبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنًا وَكَفَّلَهَا زَكَرِيَّا ۖ كُلَّمَا دَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا زَكَرِيَّا ٱلْمِحْرَابَ وَجَدَ عِندَهَا رِزْقًا ۖ قَالَ يَـٰمَرْيَمُ أَنَّىٰ لَكِ هَـٰذَا ۖ قَالَتْ هُوَ مِنْ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ ۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَرْزُقُ مَن يَشَآءُ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ٣٧﴾

Translation of the meaning

[Mention, O Muḥammad], when the wife of ʿImrān said, "My Lord, indeed I have pledged to You what is in my womb, consecrated [for Your service], so accept this from me. Indeed, You are the Hearing, the Knowing." But when she delivered her, she said, "My Lord, I have delivered a female." And Allāh was most knowing of what she delivered, and the male is not like the female. "And I have named her Mary, and I seek refuge for her in You and [for] her descendants from Satan, the expelled [from the mercy of Allāh]." So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good manner and put her in the care of Zechariah. Every time Zechariah entered upon her in the prayer chamber, he found with her provision. He said, "O Mary, from where is this [coming] to you?" She said, "It is from Allāh. Indeed, Allāh provides for whom He wills without account."

Quran · Aal Imran 3:35-37

Your family's promesa is an old and loving gesture: when someone we love is ill, we promise something in return for their health. Start with how the Quran tells it. A mother, expecting, makes a vow to God for the child she carries and asks Him to accept it. Her child is Mary. The passage says her Lord accepted her with a beautiful acceptance. A mother's vow is the first thing the story tells.

A question for you

What is a promesa, to you?

If you sayA way of showing how much I love them.
ThenThat is what Mary's mother's vow was in the passage: love turned into a promise.
If you sayA bargain with God.
ThenA bargain is close to one face of a vow. The next passage looks at a vow made as a gift, with nothing asked after it.
If you sayA tradition from my grandmother.
ThenTraditions that last across generations usually carry a real love.

Part 2 of 4

﴿فَكُلِى وَٱشْرَبِى وَقَرِّى عَيْنًا ۖ فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ مِنَ ٱلْبَشَرِ أَحَدًا فَقُولِىٓ إِنِّى نَذَرْتُ لِلرَّحْمَـٰنِ صَوْمًا فَلَنْ أُكَلِّمَ ٱلْيَوْمَ إِنسِيًّا﴾

Translation of the meaning

So eat and drink and be contented. And if you see from among humanity anyone, say, 'Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful abstention, so I will not speak today to [any] man.'"

Quran · Maryam 19:26

The Quran also tells of Mary's own vow. In a hard hour she is told to eat, to drink and be at peace, and to say to anyone she meets that she has vowed a fast to the Merciful and will not speak to anyone today. A vow here is a quiet gift made when words are not enough. The text treats it as something close to the heart of a devout woman.

A question for you

What would you give if you had nothing to give?

If you sayMy time.
ThenTime is among the dearest things to vow, because it cannot be got back.
If you sayMy silence.
ThenThat is exactly what Mary vowed in the verse.
If you sayMy attention to someone.
ThenAttention is a rare gift, and the one who receives it feels it.

Part 3 of 4

﴿وَيُطْعِمُونَ ٱلطَّعَامَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِۦ مِسْكِينًا وَيَتِيمًا وَأَسِيرًا٨ إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ لَا نُرِيدُ مِنكُمْ جَزَآءً وَلَا شُكُورًا٩﴾

Translation of the meaning

And they give food in spite of love for it[1813] to the needy, the orphan, and the captive, [Saying], "We feed you only for the face [i.e., approval] of Allāh. We wish not from you reward or gratitude.

Translator's notes

[1813] The meaning here may also be "out of love for Him," i.e., Allāh (subḥānahu wa taʿālā).

Quran · Al-Insan 76:8-9

Translation

It is well with the man who deals graciously and lends. He will maintain his cause in judgment. For he will never be shaken. The righteous will be remembered forever. He will not be afraid of evil news. His heart is steadfast, trusting in Yahweh. His heart is established. He will not be afraid in the end when he sees his adversaries. He has dispersed, he has given to the poor. His righteousness endures forever. His horn will be exalted with honor.

Original · Hebrew

טֽוֹב־אִ֭ישׁ חוֹנֵ֣ן וּמַלְוֶ֑ה יְכַלְכֵּ֖ל דְּבָרָ֣יו בְּמִשְׁפָּֽט׃ כִּֽי־לְעוֹלָ֥ם לֹא־יִמּ֑וֹט לְזֵ֥כֶר ע֝וֹלָ֗ם יִהְיֶ֥ה צַדִּֽיק׃ מִשְּׁמוּעָ֣ה רָ֭עָה לֹ֣א יִירָ֑א נָכ֥וֹן לִ֝בּ֗וֹ בָּטֻ֥חַ בַּיהוָֽה׃ סָמ֣וּךְ לִ֭בּוֹ לֹ֣א יִירָ֑א עַ֖ד אֲשֶׁר־יִרְאֶ֣ה בְצָרָֽיו׃ פִּזַּ֤ר ׀ נָ֘תַ֤ן לָאֶבְיוֹנִ֗ים צִ֭דְקָתוֹ עֹמֶ֣דֶת לָעַ֑ד קַ֝רְנ֗וֹ תָּר֥וּם בְּכָבֽוֹד׃

the Psalms · 112:5-9

World English Bible

A promesa often ends at a table: a meal for the poor, a gift to the church. This passage describes people who feed the needy, the orphan and the captive, while loving the food themselves, and who say: we feed you only for God's sake; we want from you neither reward nor thanks. These are the same people 76:7 praises for keeping their vows. This is a vow at its largest: a gift with nothing asked back, not even thanks.

A question for you

Where does your family's promise usually end?

If you sayAt a church or a shrine.
ThenIt begins in the same love as the verses, whatever the place.
If you sayAt a table with others.
ThenThat is what the two verses describe: food given for God's sake.
If you sayIn a private prayer.
ThenThe last passage speaks of exactly this kind of prayer.

Part 4 of 4

﴿وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِى عَنِّى فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ ۖ أُجِيبُ دَعْوَةَ ٱلدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ ۖ فَلْيَسْتَجِيبُوا۟ لِى وَلْيُؤْمِنُوا۟ بِى لَعَلَّهُمْ يَرْشُدُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when My servants ask you, [O Muḥammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:186

Translation

Yahweh is near to all those who call on him, to all who call on him in truth.

Original · Hebrew

קָר֣וֹב יְ֭הוָה לְכָל־קֹרְאָ֑יו לְכֹ֤ל אֲשֶׁ֖ר יִקְרָאֻ֣הוּ בֶאֱמֶֽת׃

the Psalms · 145:18

World English Bible

Behind every promesa is a question: does anyone hear us? This passage answers those who ask: I am near, and I answer the one who calls when he calls. The verse names the call, with or without a candle. A family's call at a sickbed reaches One who is already near.

A question for you

When you call in an hour of need, what do you hope for?

If you sayThat the one I love gets well.
ThenThat is the first hope, and the verse says the call is heard.
If you sayThat I am not alone.
ThenThat is what the word 'near' promises.
If you sayThat someone hears.
ThenThat is exactly the verse's answer.

The same in the other books
